question.text: How are offshore funds investing directly in Indian investee companies typically regulated by SEBI (noting that unregistered funds may invest through the FDI route under FEMA)?

answer.text: Through SEBI (FVCI) Regulations or SEBI (FPI) Regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 103), offshore fund investments in India are regulated by SEBI through Foreign Venture Capital Investor (FVCI) registration or Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) registration, depending on the asset class and strategy. The same page notes that unregistered foreign funds may instead invest through the FDI policy route, which is administered under FEMA by the RBI. The Trap: The SEBI (AIF) Regulations apply to Indian onshore AIFs, not pure offshore investors. Mutual Fund Regulations are for mutual funds. Merchant Banker Regulations are a licensing statute, not an investor-registration route. Note: FVCI registration carries source-supported benefits relevant to pre-IPO investments in India. The choice between FVCI and FPI typically depends on the asset class and investment strategy of the offshore fund.
